metadata.title: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [August 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.153

## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [August 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.153
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.153
- Datum: 08.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 3 Scans

pages.transcription:
Dear H. & M. now we are nearly ready. Our hearts are not light at all, we
do not know when we shall return as we have been here only on visitors
visas and all depends if America enters the war. Altogether it has been
a very strenuous time and especially in the last times we did not feel
happy at all. Perhaps Brazil will help us with his beauty - but I doubt
more and more if I ever shall see Bath again. Sometimes we thought
to leave everything and to go back, but I feel I shall never in my life
have more a real home - had we emigrated here like the others we
could have said, here we begin a new life, but I was bound by my nationa
lity which has and will give us still many problems. Now about Gil-
bert. Please dont take too much worries about my complicated affairs
which in future may become still more complicated, I do not want
that you take any responsability and will advise him to direct every-
thing to Dr. Artur Bondi whom your family knows from London, because
we do not know if we have not to give lectures later on in Argentine
and it will be difficult to reach us. And in the long run all will be lost
whatever one had and I am prepared to live in future from what
one earns, Brazil is much cheaper and we will have a very sober life
if possible. My book on Brazil will be forwarded to you by the Viking
press in September, I hope it will reach you safely, The Brazilian
edition is already out and the French and Spanish in preparation.
My dear Hannah and Manfred, sometimes I feel very depressed,
and doubt if we ever shall be together again, I wish only that you
shall see your child grown up and more sympathetic as ever - I
always am frightened to read that this war will take still more than
a year, this war, which has destroyed so much of our lives - I know
there are millions and millions like us, but everyone feels his own
life. I hope Manfred will have much to do in these next months
in his x ray departement - I have worked hard which means always
that I am not in a good mood. Lotte is physically much better now and
perhaps we will have in Brazil a better time: only if this nomadic life
would come to an end, I would like to live in a Negro hut in Brazil
if I should know I could stay there - and you, you have to care for
two houses. Let us hope at least that you, the young generation will

[am linken Rand, vertikal geschrieben:]
still have the reward for these enormous efforts - for me it is too late
and I could no more enjoy the victory. And you and your child will
see a better world! Yours ever Stefan
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf einem Blatt, beidseitig beschrieben (wobei die Rückseite nur durchscheinend ist). Der Text am linken Rand ist vertikal geschrieben. Die Tinte ist violett.
Rückseite des Dokuments, leer (nur durchscheinender Text der Vorderseite sichtbar).
Farbskala/Grauskala für Archivierung, über den Text gelegt.

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar, trotz der handschriftlichen Kursivschrift. Die wenigen Abkürzungen (H. & M., Dr.) sind eindeutig.
